parts.title: App map: every page, setting and guide
parts.text:
Every page, setting and guide of Clip Factory. Each block: id · where · route · title, then the answer, the steps and the buttons (action ids for show_app_buttons).

### make-clips-link · Home · / · Make clips from a YouTube, Twitch or Kick link
Copy the link to a stream or video, paste it on Home and tap **Make clips**. Clip Factory finds the best moments for you.
1. Copy the link from YouTube, Twitch or Kick.
2. Go to **Home**.
3. Tap **Paste**.
4. Tap **Make clips**.
5. Watch it work in **Jobs**. New clips wait for you in **Review**.
Buttons: make-clips-link:home (Go to Home → /)

### make-clips-upload · Home · / · Make clips from your own video file
You can make clips from a video file too. Tap **Pick a video** on Home, choose the file and tap **Make clips**. On a computer you can also drag the video onto the box.
1. Go to **Home**.
2. Tap **Pick a video**.
3. Tap the box and pick an MP4, MOV or WebM file (up to 5 GB). On a computer you can also drag the video from your folder and drop it on the box.
4. Tap **Make clips**.
Buttons: make-clips-upload:home (Go to Home → /)

### job-progress · Jobs · /jobs · Where is my job and how long does it take
Every link or video you add is one job. **Jobs** shows each one being made, step by step.
1. Tap **Jobs**.
2. Tap a job to watch its steps.
3. To stop it, tap **Stop job**. Clips already made are kept.
Buttons: job-progress:jobs (Open Jobs → /jobs)

### job-failed · Jobs › a job · /jobs · My job failed
When a job fails, open it and tap **Try again**. It starts over from the beginning and uses the video it already saved.
1. Tap **Jobs**.
2. Tap the job that failed.
3. Tap **Try again**.
Buttons: job-failed:jobs (Open Jobs → /jobs)

### delete-job · Jobs · /jobs · Delete a job
Tap the bin on a job in **Jobs**, or tap **Delete job** on its page. Clip Factory asks first and says what happens. A job still working stops first. Clips you kept or posted stay, and your posts stay up. Its clips waiting in Review go too only if you turn on **Also delete its clips in Review**. You can undo for 8 seconds.
1. Tap **Jobs**.
2. Tap the bin on the job, or tap **Select** to pick several (**Pick all failed** picks every failed one).
3. Tap **Delete job**.
Buttons: delete-job:jobs (Open Jobs → /jobs)

### jobs-running · Jobs · /jobs · Is anything running right now
**Jobs** shows what Clip Factory is making right now.
1. Tap **Jobs** to see each job and how far along it is.
Buttons: jobs-running:jobs (Open Jobs → /jobs)

### review-keep · Review · /review · What Upload does
**Upload** says yes to a clip. It goes up to every place you picked under **Upload to**, each with its own caption. Nothing is posted until you tap **Upload**.
1. Tap **Review**.
2. Under **Upload to**, turn on each place you want.
3. Tap **Upload** to post it, or **Throw away** if you do not like it.
Buttons: review-keep:review (Open Review → /review)

### review-upload-to · Review › a clip › Upload to · /review · Upload to many places at once
On each clip, **Upload to** shows every place that is set up, all ticked to start. Tap **Use my settings**, then **Upload**. That is the only place picker: each ticked place gets its own row below for its words and options. A place that is not set up yet does not show; set it up in **Set up posting**.
1. Tap **Review**.
2. Under **Upload to**, tap a place to untick it if it should not go there.
3. Tap **Use my settings**, then **Upload**.
Buttons: review-upload-to:review (Open Review → /review)

### review-use-my-settings · Review › a clip › Use my settings · /review · Use my settings: upload in two taps
**Use my settings** puts your saved choices on every ticked place: who can see it, comments, duets and stitches, never made for kids. TikTok needs your own tap each time, so tap it, then tap **Upload**. Change a place for one clip in its row.
1. Tap **Review**.
2. Tap **Use my settings**. It says **Your settings are on**.
3. Tap **Upload**.
Buttons: review-use-my-settings:review (Open Review → /review)

### review-place-rows · Review › a clip › a place's row · /review · Change one place for one clip
Each ticked place has its own row under **Use my settings**. Tap the row to open its words and options. For a paid partnership, open **TikTok**, turn on **Commercial content** and tick **Branded content**.
1. Tap **Review**.
2. Tap a place's row, like **TikTok · caption and settings**.
3. Change what you want, then tap **Upload**.
Buttons: review-place-rows:review (Open Review → /review)

### my-settings · Settings › Posting › My settings · /settings/posting/my-settings#my-settings-tiktok · Change My settings
**My settings** are the choices **Use my settings** puts on a clip, one part per place, X too. They start at everyone can see it, comments, duets and stitches on, and never made for kids.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **My settings**.
3. Change a place. It saves at once.
Buttons: my-settings:open (Open My settings → /settings/posting/my-settings#my-settings-tiktok)

### review-throw-away · Review · /review · Throw away a clip, and Undo
Tap **Throw away** on a clip you do not want. Changed your mind? Tap **Undo** within 8 seconds and it comes back.
1. Tap **Review**.
2. Tap **Throw away** on the clip.
3. Oops? Tap **Undo** on the message at the bottom, within 8 seconds.
Buttons: review-throw-away:review (Open Review → /review)

### review-captions · Review › a clip › captions · /review · Change a caption before Upload
Each clip has its own caption for every place it goes. Change them on the clip in **Review** before you tap **Upload**. They save by themselves.
1. Tap **Review**.
2. Tap the place's row, like **TikTok · caption and settings**.
3. Type your new caption.
4. Tap **Upload** when it looks right.
Buttons: review-captions:review (Open Review → /review)

### review-chat-went-wild · Review · /review · What Chat went wild means
Each clip card says **Why:** it was picked. **Chat went wild** means the stream's chat suddenly went much faster than usual, or lots of people typed the same thing, right after this moment. Clip Factory only trusts it when something is also seen or heard there.
1. Tap **Review**.
2. Look under the clip for **Why:**.
3. **Chat went wild** means the viewers loved this moment.
Buttons: review-chat-went-wild:review (Open Review → /review)

### review-waiting · Review · /review · How many clips are waiting in Review
New clips wait in **Review** until you **Upload** or **Throw away** each one.
1. Tap **Review** to check them one by one.
Buttons: review-waiting:review (Open Review → /review)

### clip-posting-failed · Library · /library · Uploading a clip did not work
If one place did not work, the clip in **Library** says **Didn't work** with the reason, and that place has its own **Try again**.
1. Tap **Library**.
2. Find the place that says **Didn't work**.
3. Tap **Try again** next to it.
Buttons: clip-posting-failed:review (Open Library → /library)

### clip-performance · Library › a clip · /library · See how a clip is doing
Open a clip in **Library** to see its views, likes and comments on each place it was posted. A crown marks where it did best.
1. Tap **Library**.
2. Tap the clip.
3. Scroll to see each place and its numbers.
Buttons: clip-performance:library (Open Library → /library)

### real-money · Money · /money · How much money did I make?
Clip Factory only shows money a place reports. It never guesses from views and you never type money in. Tap **Money** in the menu. **All your money** at the top adds up your last 30 days from every place, Content Rewards too. **Monthly MRR** under it is the apps only. The list further down shows what YouTube says each posted clip earned. TikTok, Instagram and X don't share money with apps.
1. Tap **Money** in the menu.
2. Read **All your money** at the top. Each amount says whose numbers it is.
3. Scroll down to see what each clip earned.
Buttons: real-money:money (Open Money → /money); real-money:clips (See each clip → /money)

### money-mrr · Money · /money · What is MRR on the Money page?
MRR usually means subscriptions. Here it means the money the apps reported for your videos: **Monthly MRR** is the last 30 days, **Weekly MRR** the last 7, **Daily MRR** a normal day lately and **Yearly MRR** the monthly money kept up for a year (**at this pace**). Pick apps with the icons at the bottom right.
1. Tap **Money** in the menu.
2. Tap app icons in the bar at the bottom right to pick apps. **All** shows every app.
3. Tap **7 days**, **30 days**, **90 days** or **Year** to change the chart and the clip list.
4. Content Rewards money is not in MRR. It is in **All your money** at the top.
Buttons: money-mrr:money (Open Money → /money); money-mrr:filter (Pick apps → /money)

### money-progress · Settings › Posting › Money · /settings/posting/money#money-youtube · Am I monetized yet?
Open **Settings › Posting › Money**. Each app's card has a pill: **Earning**, **In the program**, **Not yet**, **Goal reached**, **Can't tell** or **Not shared**, and bars like 812 / 1,000 subscribers. Only YouTube tells apps if you're in its paid program. **Goal reached** means you hit the numbers, but the app also checks things Clip Factory can't see.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **Money**.
3. Look at each app's pill and bars.
4. Tap **More** to see the other goals.
Buttons: money-progress:money (Open Money → /settings/posting/money#money-youtube)

### money-allow · Settings › Posting › Money › YouTube · /settings/posting/money#money-youtube · Let Clip Factory read your YouTube money
On the YouTube card, press **Allow money reading** and say yes on Google's page. A grown-up first adds the money permission in the same Google Cloud project (no new keys) and sets Publishing status to **In production**. Google's "unverified app" screen is normal: press **Advanced**, then **Continue**. Your connection and posts stay as they are.
1. Tap **Settings**, then **Posting**, then **Money**.
2. On the YouTube card, tap **First time? Steps for a grown-up** and do the steps.
3. Tap **Allow money reading**.
4. On Google's page, tap **Allow**.
Buttons: money-allow:money (Open the YouTube card → /settings/posting/money#money-youtube)

### money-payouts · Settings › Posting › Money › Getting your money out · /settings/posting/money#money-payouts · Where do I add my bank account to get paid?
Each app pays you itself, so you add your bank account or PayPal inside each app. YouTube: **AdSense for YouTube › Payments**. Facebook and Instagram: Meta's payout settings. TikTok: your TikTok **Balance**. X: **Monetization**, through Stripe. Clip Factory never needs your bank details, and never asks for them.
1. Tap **Settings**, then **Posting**, then **Money**.
2. Scroll to **Getting your money out**.
3. Open that app and add your bank or PayPal there.
Buttons: money-payouts:money (Open payouts help → /settings/posting/money#money-payouts)

### money-everywhere · Money · /money · How much did I earn everywhere?
Tap **Money**. The first card, **All your money**, adds up the last 30 days from YouTube, Content Rewards and every other place that tells apps what you earn. **Total** is the biggest number. Each amount says whose numbers it is. TikTok, Instagram and X say **Not available**, never $0. Dollars and euros are never added together.
1. Tap **Money** in the menu.
2. Look at **All your money**, the first card.
3. Read **Total** and the places in it.
4. Under Content Rewards, read **Right now** and **Earned so far**.
Buttons: money-everywhere:money (Open Money → /money)

### money-not-available · Money · /money · Why does it say Not available from TikTok?
TikTok, Instagram and X don't tell apps what you earn. So Clip Factory never guesses and never shows $0: it says **Not available from TikTok** and where to look. TikTok: **Profile**, then **Balance**. Instagram: **Professional dashboard**, then **Payouts**. X: **Monetization**. Facebook says **Coming soon** for now.
1. Tap **Money** in the menu.
2. Find the place in **All your money**.
3. Read its **Look in** line.
4. Open that app and look there.
5. Money that went to your bank? Content Rewards doesn't tell apps. Look on Whop, **Balances**.
Buttons: money-not-available:money (Open Money → /money)

### clip-views · Library › a clip · /library · How many views does this clip have
A clip's page in **Library** adds up its views from every place it was posted.
1. Tap **Library**.
2. Tap the clip to see its views.
Buttons: clip-views:library (Open Library → /library)

### clips-posted · Library · /library · How many clips have I posted
**Library** lists every clip you uploaded.
1. Tap **Library**.
Buttons: clips-posted:library (Open Library → /library)

### refresh-numbers · Library › a clip · /library · Refresh numbers
Numbers update by themselves. To check now, open the clip and tap **Refresh numbers**. If it says **Next check in**, wait that long. Instagram and Facebook can take 2 days to settle.
1. Tap **Library**.
2. Tap the clip.
3. Tap **Refresh numbers**.
Buttons: refresh-numbers:library (Open Library → /library)

### this-week-best · Library › This week · /library · Star the best clips of the week
In **Library**, tap **This week** and star the clips that did best with **Best this week**. Clip Factory learns from your stars and makes more clips like them.
1. Tap **Library**.
2. Tap **This week**.
3. Tap the star on your best clips (up to 10).
Buttons: this-week-best:week (Open This week → /library?view=week)

### learn-from-clips · Settings › Clip making › What it learned · /settings/clip-making/learned · How Clip Factory learns from your clips
Every day Clip Factory checks your clips 7 days after posting. When some clips did much better than normal for that streamer, it looks at what they share and writes a short lesson. Lessons it is sure about go to your skills as **Prior learnings**. You can turn a lesson off or delete it in **What it learned**.
1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Clip making**.
3. Tap **What it learned**.
4. Tap **Turn off** or **Delete** on a lesson you do not like.
Buttons: learn-from-clips:open (Open What it learned → /settings/clip-making/learned)

### follow-streamers · Settings › Clip making › Streamers I follow · /settings/clip-making/streamers · Follow streamers and see who is live
Open **Streamers I follow** and paste a streamer's link or type their name. If you type a name, tap **YouTube**, **Twitch** or **Kick**. Only follow streamers who said you can clip them: tap **Yes, they said I can**, then **Follow**. You see who is **LIVE** and when a stream ended or a new video came out. Making clips by itself comes in the next update; each video costs the same as one you paste.
1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Clip making**.
3. Tap **Streamers I follow**.
4. Paste a link or type a name, then tap **Find**.
5. Tap **Yes, they said I can**, then **Follow**.
Buttons: follow-streamers:open (Open Streamers → /settings/clip-making/streamers)

### streamer-keys · Settings › Clip making › Streamers I follow › Twitch and Kick keys · /settings/clip-making/streamers · Twitch and Kick keys for live badges
YouTube works without keys. To see when Twitch or Kick streamers are live, a grown-up makes a free app on dev.twitch.tv or kick.com once and pastes its two keys in **Twitch and Kick keys**. Until then the streamer shows **Needs a grown-up**, but you can still follow them. Removing keys needs a long press.
1. Open **Streamers I follow**.
2. Find **Twitch and Kick keys**.
3. Ask a grown-up to tap **I am the grown-up** and follow the steps.
4. Tap **Save keys**, then **Check it**.
Buttons: streamer-keys:open (Open the keys → /settings/clip-making/streamers)

### best-clip-week-views · Library › This week · /library · Views on my best clip this week
**This week** in **Library** shows this week's clips, most views first.
1. Tap **Library**.
2. Tap **This week**.
Buttons: best-clip-week-views:week (See this week → /library?view=week)

### week-total-views · Library › This week · /library · Total views this week
**This week** in **Library** adds up the views of this week's clips.
1. Tap **Library**.
2. Tap **This week**.
Buttons: week-total-views:week (See this week → /library?view=week)

### week-clips · Library › This week · /library · How many clips this week
**This week** in **Library** lists the clips from this week.
1. Tap **Library**.
2. Tap **This week**.
Buttons: week-clips:week (See this week → /library?view=week)

### tiktok-private · Settings › Posting › Set up posting › TikTok · /settings/posting/setup/tiktok · Why my clip is private on TikTok
TikTok shows posts from Clip Factory privately until Clip Factory's TikTok app is approved. Your clip is posted, only you can see it for now, and its numbers come after.
1. Open the clip in **Library**.
2. TikTok says **Uploaded privately**. That is normal for now.
Buttons: tiktok-private:library (Open Library → /library)

### tiktok-app-review · Settings › Posting › Set up posting › TikTok · /settings/posting/setup/tiktok · TikTok won't let me press Save
On TikTok's app page, **Save** stays off until **App review** has its text and a video. Copy the review text in TikTok setup step 13, add a short screen video, then Save. Display API is not a product any more: add video.list and user.info.stats with **Add scopes** under Login Kit.
1. Open TikTok setup, step 13.
2. Copy the review text into **App review**.
3. Upload a short screen video.
4. Press **Save**.
Buttons: tiktok-app-review:page (Set up TikTok → /settings/posting/setup/tiktok)

### posting-setup-youtube · Settings › Posting › Set up posting › YouTube · /settings/posting/setup/youtube · Connect YouTube
Open **Set up posting** and tap **YouTube**. Follow its steps one by one: make your key, paste it, then tap **Connect YouTube**. You do it once, then Clip Factory posts there by itself.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **Set up posting**.
3. Tap **YouTube**.
4. Do each step in order.
5. Tap **Connect YouTube**.
Buttons: posting-setup-youtube:list (Open Set up posting → /settings/posting/setup); posting-setup-youtube:page (Set up YouTube → /settings/posting/setup/youtube)

### posting-setup-instagram · Settings › Posting › Set up posting › Instagram · /settings/posting/setup/instagram · Connect Instagram
Open **Set up posting** and tap **Instagram**. Follow its steps one by one: make your key, paste it, then tap **Connect Instagram**. You do it once, then Clip Factory posts there by itself.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **Set up posting**.
3. Tap **Instagram**.
4. Do each step in order.
5. Tap **Connect Instagram**.
Buttons: posting-setup-instagram:list (Open Set up posting → /settings/posting/setup); posting-setup-instagram:page (Set up Instagram → /settings/posting/setup/instagram)

### posting-setup-facebook · Settings › Posting › Set up posting › Facebook · /settings/posting/setup/facebook · Connect Facebook
Open **Set up posting** and tap **Facebook**. Follow its steps one by one: make your key, paste it, then tap **Connect Facebook**. You do it once, then Clip Factory posts there by itself.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **Set up posting**.
3. Tap **Facebook**.
4. Do each step in order.
5. Tap **Connect Facebook**.
Buttons: posting-setup-facebook:list (Open Set up posting → /settings/posting/setup); posting-setup-facebook:page (Set up Facebook → /settings/posting/setup/facebook)

### posting-setup-tiktok · Settings › Posting › Set up posting › TikTok · /settings/posting/setup/tiktok · Connect TikTok
Open **Set up posting** and tap **TikTok**. Follow its steps one by one: make your key, paste it, then tap **Connect TikTok**. You do it once, then Clip Factory posts there by itself.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **Set up posting**.
3. Tap **TikTok**.
4. Do each step in order.
5. Tap **Connect TikTok**.
Buttons: posting-setup-tiktok:list (Open Set up posting → /settings/posting/setup); posting-setup-tiktok:page (Set up TikTok → /settings/posting/setup/tiktok)

### posting-setup-x · Settings › Posting › Set up posting › X · /settings/posting/setup/x · Connect X
Open **Set up posting** and tap **X**. Follow its steps one by one: make your key, paste it, then tap **Connect X**. You do it once, then Clip Factory posts there by itself.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **Set up posting**.
3. Tap **X**.
4. Do each step in order.
5. Tap **Connect X**.
Buttons: posting-setup-x:list (Open Set up posting → /settings/posting/setup); posting-setup-x:page (Set up X → /settings/posting/setup/x)

### accounts-connected · Settings › Posting › Set up posting · /settings/posting/setup#setup-posting · Which accounts are connected
**Set up posting** shows how many of the five places are ready, and a card for each one.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **Set up posting**.
Buttons: accounts-connected:setup (Open Set up posting → /settings/posting/setup#setup-posting)

### setup-list-gone · Settings › Posting › Set up posting · /settings/posting/setup#setup-todo · Where did my setup list go?
The **Set up posting** list sits at the top right until each place is set up or skipped. When all five are done or skipped, it says **All set!** and goes away. It comes back by itself if a place you set up needs you again. You can always find every place, skip one, or bring back one you skipped in **Settings › Posting › Set up posting**.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **Set up posting**.
3. Find the place you skipped. It says **Skipped**.
4. Tap **Un-skip** to put it back on the list, or tap its card to set it up now.
Buttons: setup-list-gone:setup (Open Set up posting → /settings/posting/setup#setup-todo)

### where-clips-go · Settings › Posting › Where clips go · /settings/posting/where#post-to · Which places start switched on
In **Where clips go** you pick the places that start switched on for new clips. On each clip you can still turn places on or off under **Upload to**.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **Where clips go**.
3. Turn each place on or off.
Buttons: where-clips-go:where (Open Where clips go → /settings/posting/where#post-to)

### x-costs · Settings › Posting › Set up posting › X · /settings/posting/setup/x#x-cost · What X charges for numbers
X charges a little for every number check. The checks stop at $10 a month, so X never costs more.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Posting**, then **Set up posting**.
3. Tap **X** and read **What X costs**.
Buttons: x-costs:setup (Open X setup → /settings/posting/setup/x#x-cost)

### skills-add · Settings › Clip making › Skills · /settings/clip-making/skills#add-skill · Add a skill
In Skills, tap **Write a skill** and answer three easy questions. Or tap **Upload a file** to add a SKILL.md or a .zip with one inside.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Clip making**, then **Skills**.
3. Tap **Write a skill**, or **Upload a file**.
Buttons: skills-add:skills (Open Skills → /settings/clip-making/skills#add-skill); skills-add:write (Write a skill → /settings/clip-making/skills/new)

### skills-what · Settings › Clip making › Skills · /settings/clip-making/skills#your-skills · What a skill is
A skill teaches Clip Factory how you like your clips. All the AI in Clip Factory uses every skill, every time. To stop using one, open it and tap **Delete**. Built-in skills stay.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Clip making**, then **Skills**.
3. Tap a skill to read it, edit it or delete it.
Buttons: skills-what:skills (Open Skills → /settings/clip-making/skills#your-skills)

### skills-write · Settings › Clip making › Skills › Write a skill · /settings/clip-making/skills/new · Make your own skill
Tap **Write a skill**. Answer the three questions: a name, when to use it, and what Clip Factory should do. Tap **Use the example** if you are stuck. Then tap **Save skill**.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Clip making**, then **Skills**.
3. Tap **Write a skill**.
4. Answer the three questions.
5. Tap **Save skill**.
Buttons: skills-write:new (Write a skill → /settings/clip-making/skills/new)

### skills-edit · Settings › Clip making › Skills · /settings/clip-making/skills#your-skills · Edit a skill
Open **Skills** and tap the skill. Tap **Edit**, change the words, then tap **Save changes**. Built-in skills can be read, not changed.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Clip making**, then **Skills**.
3. Tap the skill.
4. Tap **Edit**.
5. Tap **Save changes**.
Buttons: skills-edit:skills (Open Skills → /settings/clip-making/skills#your-skills)

### skills-delete · Settings › Clip making › Skills · /settings/clip-making/skills#your-skills · Delete a skill
To throw away a skill, open **Skills** and tap the skill. Tap **Delete**, then **Delete** again. Changed your mind? Tap **Undo** at the bottom. Built-in skills cannot be deleted.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Clip making**, then **Skills**.
3. Tap the skill.
4. Tap **Delete**, then **Delete** again.
Buttons: skills-delete:skills (Open Skills → /settings/clip-making/skills#your-skills)

### sounds-click · Settings › Look & feel › Sounds · /settings/look-and-feel/sounds#click-sound · Change the click sound
Pick your **Click sound** in Settings › Look & feel › Sounds. There are 30 to choose from. Tap a card to hear it.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Look & feel**, then **Sounds**.
3. Under **Click sound**, tap a card to hear it and pick it.
Buttons: sounds-click:sounds (Open Sounds → /settings/look-and-feel/sounds#click-sound)

### sounds-error · Settings › Look & feel › Sounds · /settings/look-and-feel/sounds#error-sound · Change the error sound
Pick your **Error sound** in Settings › Look & feel › Sounds. There are 30 to choose from. Tap a card to hear it.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Look & feel**, then **Sounds**.
3. Under **Error sound**, tap a card to hear it and pick it.
Buttons: sounds-error:sounds (Open Sounds → /settings/look-and-feel/sounds#error-sound)

### sounds-off · Settings › Look & feel › Sounds · /settings/look-and-feel/sounds#sounds-on · Turn sounds off or on
Use the **Sounds** switch in Settings › Look & feel › Sounds to turn every sound off or on.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Look & feel**, then **Sounds**.
3. Tap the **Sounds** switch.
Buttons: sounds-off:sounds (Open Sounds → /settings/look-and-feel/sounds#sounds-on)

### motion-and-background · Settings › Look & feel · /settings/look-and-feel/motion#reduce-motion · Make it calmer: Reduce motion and Background
Turn on **Reduce motion** to stop confetti, page moves and the moving background. In **Background** you can pick plain **Colours** instead of the glass or a picture.
1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Tap **Look & feel**.
3. Tap **Motion** and turn on **Reduce motion**.

## Setting up posting, per platform (docs/SETUP_POSTING.md)

# Set up posting

Clip Factory can post your clips by itself to **YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and X**. For that, each of the
five needs to be set up **once**. This page is the same list of steps the app shows you in **Settings › Posting ›
Set up posting**, word for word in meaning and in the same order, so you can read ahead or print it.

**Steps checked on 19 Nov 2026** against each platform's own help pages (the list is at the
[end of this page](#research-sources-checked-on-16-nov-2026), with what changed on 19 Nov 2026 below it). Platforms sometimes rename a button. When that happens, the app
shows an "If you see…" hint, and the [maintainer notes](#for-maintainers-keeping-the-app-and-this-page-in-step) say how to
update both.

You never write code. You only use the Clip Factory app and the platforms' own websites.

## The setup list

Do each one once. After that Clip Factory posts by itself. You can do them in any order and stop at any time: the app
remembers where you were and opens the next step for you.

| # | Platform | Time | Cost | What you need first | Good to know |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [YouTube](#youtube) | about 20 minutes | Free | A Google account with a YouTube channel | Posts are public straight away. |
| 2 | [TikTok](#tiktok) | about 40 minutes, then TikTok checks your app (days) | Free | A TikTok account | Posts may stay **"Only me"** for a long time. TikTok often says no to apps that only one person uses. |
| 3 | [Instagram](#instagram) | about 25 minutes | Free | An Instagram **Creator** or **Business** account linked to a Facebook **Page**, and a Facebook account | Reels may be seen only by you until the app is **Live**. |
| 4 | [Facebook](#facebook) | about 25 minutes | Free | A Facebook **Page** you fully control | Reels may be seen only by you until the app is **Live**. |
| 5 | [X](#x) | about 15 minutes | **Costs a little**: about $1.50 for 100 clips | An X account and a grown-up's card | X charges for every post. Clip Factory stops at $10 a month. |

The ring at the top of Set up posting says how many are ready, for example **2 of 5 ready**. A **Set up posting**
list also stays at the top right of every page (a small pill on phones) with **Set up** and **Skip** for each
platform. It goes away when each one is ready or skipped, and you can always skip one or bring it back here in
Settings.

**Get paid by brands.** Under the five cards sits one more card, **Content Rewards**, for paid clipping campaigns. It
is set up once too (3 steps), but it is not a place Clip Factory posts to, so it never counts in **2 of 5 ready** and
is never in the floating list. Its steps are in [Content Rewards](#content-rewards) below.

## How every setup works

Every platform page has the same four parts:

1. **Get ready**: what your account needs before you start.
2. **Make your {Platform} key**: a few clicks on the platform's developer website. You do this once.
3. **Connect**: one big button. You say yes on the platform and come back to Clip Factory.
4. **Go public**: what the platform still has to allow, and how it is going.

Each step is a big numbered card. The numbers run on from one part to the next. A card has only what that step needs:

| On the card | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Open {site}** | Opens the right page of the platform in a new tab. Come back to the Clip Factory tab after. |
| **Copy** | Copies a value (a name, a web address). You see **Copied!**. Then paste it on the platform. |
| A paste box with **Paste** | Where you put a key from the platform. The box checks it while you type and says what is wrong. |
| An upload box | Only on TikTok: where you drop the file TikTok gives you. |
| **If you see…** | What to do when the platform looks a little different. |
| **I did this** | Press it when you finished the step. The next step opens. |

Some steps tick themselves (for example when your keys are saved or when you are connected). Steps marked **(only if
you need it)** are extra and do not count in the ring.

There is always **one** vermilion-red button on the screen: it is the next thing to press.

**Use a computer.** The developer websites work best on a computer. Use the same browser for every step, and keep
Clip Factory open in one tab and the platform in another.

### The values Clip Factory gives you

The answers, word for word. They are all true today: do not change them to sound bigger.

- **Organization name**: Clip Factory
- **Organization website**: your About page (the Website URL from step 8)
- **Organization description**:

> Clip Factory is my own clipping tool, for me as one creator. Today I am its only user. Sign-up is invite-only, so it is not open to the public.
>
> There is no company. Clip Factory is the name of my tool, and I am one person.
>
> It turns long videos and streams I pick into short vertical clips. The sources are my own gameplay recordings and other creators' streams and videos, including paid clipping campaigns (such as Content Rewards), where a creator pays clippers to post clips of their content. I treat campaign clips as paid partnerships and mark them as Branded content.
>
> I watch every clip and post only the ones I approve, to my own TikTok account, which I connected myself with Login Kit.

- **How you use Direct Post**:

> Clip Factory uses Direct Post to post one clip to my own TikTok account when I press Upload. Nothing posts by itself.
>
> Before each post it asks TikTok for my creator info and shows my nickname and picture. I pick who can see it from TikTok's own options; nothing is picked for me. Comments, Duet and Stitch start off, and a setting I turned off in TikTok stays off and grey. I can turn on Commercial content and pick Your brand, Branded content or both; Branded content can't be Only me. I can edit the caption. TikTok's Music Usage Confirmation (and the Branded Content Policy for branded content) shows above Upload. A clip longer than TikTok allows for me can't be posted.
>
> After Upload, Clip Factory sends the video file, tells me TikTok can take a few minutes, and checks the post status until it is posted.
>
> A Use my settings button puts my saved TikTok choices on with one tap of mine, per clip. Opening the TikTok row shows every option.
>
> Other scopes: user.info.basic shows my name and picture. video.list shows the views and likes of my own posts. user.info.stats shows my follower count on my Money page, only after I say OK.

- **How you got the number**:

> Clip Factory has one user: me. Sign-up is invite-only, so at most 1 creator posts with it on any day, up to about 15 clips, which is TikTok's own daily limit for one creator. So I picked the smallest choice.

- **Data you store**:

> Clip Factory stores this TikTok data, for my one account only:
> - open_id
> - access token and refresh token (in AWS Secrets Manager, encrypted at rest), and when they expire
> - the scopes I granted
> - username, display name and avatar URL
> - for each post: publish_id, the privacy level I picked, the post status, TikTok's post id, and the error if a post fails
> - the caption I wrote
> - views, likes, comments and shares of my own posts (video.list)
> - a total of views and a count of long videos from my recent videos (video.list)
> - my follower count (user.info.stats, only after I say OK)
> Disconnect revokes the token and deletes it.

- Only after the form in step 24 passes: turn **Private account** off again.
- Posts from before stay private. To show one, change it to **Everyone** in the TikTok app.
- TikTok still allows about 15 posts a day.

## Content Rewards

Get paid by brands for your clips. About 10 minutes · Free · Steps checked on 21 Nov 2026.

Content Rewards (contentrewards.com) is where brands pay clippers for views. You pick a campaign there and join it.
Then you paste its link into Clip Factory. Clip Factory reads the campaign's rules and follows them on every clip:
the length, the hashtags and tags, "#Ad" first in the caption, "Paid partnership" on the video, the logo, which
videos you may clip, and the places the campaign pays for. After each post, Clip Factory sends the clip to Content
Rewards for you. Whop is the website where Content Rewards sends your money. From there it goes to your bank.

Content Rewards is **not** one of the five places above. In Settings › Posting › Set up posting it has its own
card under the five, in a part called "Get paid by brands". It never counts in "2 of 5 ready" and is never in the

the campaign money on the "Money" page (`/money#content-rewards`). It is switched on. If it is ever switched off
for your app, the card says "Coming soon".

### Part 4: Check each clip

Each campaign clip gets one line next to its post, on the clip page, in Library, on the job page and on the campaign
card. Content Rewards only takes a clip in its first 30 minutes, so Clip Factory sends it the moment it is live.

| The line says | What it means |
|---|---|
| "Goes to Content Rewards after it posts." | It isn't posted yet. |
| "Sending to Content Rewards…" | Clip Factory is sending it. |
| "Sent ✓ · Waiting for the brand to check it" | It is in. The brand checks it. |
| "On hold: Content Rewards is checking the views." | Content Rewards checks the views first. |
| "Approved ✓ · 12.3K views on YouTube" | The brand said yes. "Earned on Content Rewards: $3.10 so far." shows once it has earned money. |
| "Not approved: “…”" | The brand said no, with its reason (or "The brand gave no reason."). A "Next time: …" hint may follow. Tap "Ask again". |
| "Asked again ✓ · The answer takes 2 to 7 days." | You asked again. Wait. |
| "Back in review after you asked again." | The brand looks again. |
| "Send this to Content Rewards now (12 min left)" | Clip Factory couldn't send it. Send it yourself (below). |
| "You sent it ✓ · Looking for it on Content Rewards…" | Clip Factory looks for it by its link. |
| "Too late to send this one. …" | More than 30 minutes went by. Next time, send it as soon as Clip Factory reminds you. |
| "Content Rewards didn't take it: …" | The reason and the button to fix it are on the line. |
| "Content Rewards took this clip off the campaign. It earns nothing more." | Nothing to do. |
| "The post is gone from YouTube, so it stops earning." | Nothing to do. |

If the line says "YouTube didn't take the Paid promotion switch. #Ad and the words on the video still tell viewers.",
nothing to do.

Views on the line are Content Rewards' count of the post's views. They are not the views a campaign pays for. Money
on the line is only what Content Rewards itself reports, never a rate times views.

### Part 5: Move your money to Whop

The Money page has a Content Rewards part. Whop is the website where Content Rewards sends your money. From there it
goes to your bank.

It shows three tiles, all Content Rewards' own numbers, never a guess:
- "Still earning": clips still earning. The amount can still change. (On Content Rewards: **Queued** and
  **Arriving**.)
- "On its way": moving to your Whop balance.
- "Ready to move": you can move this to Whop now. (On Content Rewards: **Balance**.)

Then "Content Rewards paid you $62.40 so far · last money Tue 18 Nov", a line per campaign, and "Content Rewards'
numbers · checked 20 min ago". While it reads everything for the first time the total says "Checking…". Clips the
brand hasn't checked yet show $0 until the brand says yes.

First, one question, asked once: "Do you see **Finance** in the Content Rewards menu?" Tap "Yes" or "No". "Change my
answer" asks again. When "Ready to move" is $1.00 or more, "Move your money to Whop" is the red step.

**If you said No**, link Whop once:

#### Link your Whop account
Once.
- No Whop account? Tap **Open Whop** and make one with the same email.
- Tap "Open Content Rewards settings". Find Connect your Whop account and tap **Open Whop**.
- Sign in to Whop and allow it. Then come back. Tap "I did this".
- Can't find it? Tap **Profile** and look again. "Could not open Whop. Try again.": tap **Open Whop** again. "already
  connected to another creator": use your own Whop account, or ask Content Rewards support.

**If you said Yes**, set up payouts once:

#### Set up payouts
Once.
- Tap "Open Content Rewards". Tap **Finance** in the menu. You'll see **Set up payouts**.
- Do each one: **Verify your identity**, **Set your tax handling**, **Turn on two-factor auth**, **Add a bank
  account**.
- Some open on Whop. Tap **Continue on Whop**, finish there, then come back. Tap "I did this".
- "Your details are in review with Whop": nothing to do, wait a day or two. "Setup session expired": tap **Continue on
  Whop** again. "Payouts are turned off": ask Content Rewards support.

**Then, each time** (No or Yes):

#### Move money to Whop
Each time.
- Tap the "Amount" chip to copy it (for example 18.25). Tap "Open Earnings".
- Tap **Withdraw**. Paste the amount in **Amount**. It must be $1.00 or more.
- Tap **Withdraw** again.
- It says the money is on its way to your Whop balance. It usually takes minutes. The step ticks itself.

| "Minimum withdrawal is $1.00." | Wait until you have $1 or more. |
| "Connect payout account in Settings" | Do the step above: link Whop. |

## What Clip Factory does (docs/BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md)

## Functional requirements

### BR-01 Add a video by link
The owner can start a job by pasting a link to a YouTube video, a YouTube stream (live or past), a Twitch VOD or a
Kick VOD.
- AC1: The New job screen accepts `youtube.com`, `youtu.be`, `twitch.tv` and `kick.com` links and shows the detected platform before starting.
- AC2: Any other link is refused with a plain message, before a job is created.
- AC3: `POST /v1/jobs` with `{ "source": { "type": "link", "url" } }` returns `201` and a job in `queued`.

### BR-02 Add a video by upload
The owner can upload a video file instead of a link ("I need to be able to upload").
- AC1: Files up to 5 GB of any `video/*` type can be uploaded from phone or desktop.
- AC2: The upload goes straight to S3 with a presigned URL (no file passes through a Lambda) and shows progress.
- AC3: A finished upload can be turned into a job (`source.type = "upload"`).

### BR-03 Cloud agent cuts the clips
An AI agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, running Claude Fable 5.1, processes each job in the cloud.
- AC1: The agent runs on AgentCore Runtime (`cf_prod_clip_agent`) and calls Claude Fable 5.1 through Amazon Bedrock.
- AC2: The job runs without the owner's computer being on.
- AC3: The job goes through the steps resolve, download, transcribe, analyze, select, render, checklist, captions,
  finalize, and the app shows each step's status live (pushed over the WebSocket API within seconds, NFR-13; polling
  only while disconnected).

### BR-04 Between 5 and 10 viral clips per job
- AC1: Each finished job has between `clipMin` and `clipMax` clips (defaults 5 and 10; the owner can change both
  in Settings, within 1–10). The agent chooses how many within the range from what the source offers.
- AC2: When the source cannot give the minimum (for example a short video), the job still finishes with what it found
  and says so plainly.
- AC3: Each clip carries a moment type (rage, chaos, interaction, no-way, first reaction, hot take), a score from 1 to 10
  and a one-line reason.

### BR-05 Clips follow best practice from the owner's skills
"Clip them up into viral segments with the best practices based on the skill that I'm going to give you."
- AC1: Every clip is vertical 1080×1920, 20–45 seconds unless a skill says otherwise, with a 6–8 word text hook,
  burned-in captions and a cover image.
- AC2: Each clip runs the pre-post checklist from the skills (section D of the built-in playbook) and shows
  every item as pass or fail. A failing clip gets one fix pass or is replaced by a spare moment.
- AC3: Each clip has a caption for every platform: YouTube title and description, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and X.

### BR-06 Skills in Settings: add, read, change, delete
"I should be able to attach skills in the settings of this application." Updated by the owner on 2026-11-16: "I want
to be able to create, read, update, delete skills in Settings, following the trees, branches, apples, leaves
structure." ([CONTRACTS.md §18](CONTRACTS.md#18-skills-full-create-read-update-delete-every-ai-call-uses-every-skill-owner-request-2026-11-16),
[the skill pages](UX_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#skill-pages))
- AC1: **Create.** In Settings › Clip making › Skills the owner can **write** a skill by answering three questions
  ("What is the skill called?", "When should Clip Factory use it?", "What should it do?"), or **upload** a `SKILL.md`
  (≤ 1 MB) or a `.zip` that contains one `SKILL.md` (≤ 20 MB). Two skills cannot have the same name; the app says so
  under the first question.
- AC2: **Read.** Every skill (built-in and the owner's) is listed with its title, when it is used, an **Always used**
  badge, a **Built in** badge where it applies, its size and the date it last changed. Tapping a skill opens its own
  page, which shows the whole skill as formatted text (and, for a `.zip`, the other files in it). Nothing in a skill
  can run code in the app.
- AC3: **Update.** The owner can change any of their own skills with the same three questions, or replace its whole
  file with a new upload. If the skill was changed somewhere else in the meantime, the app says so and offers "Use the
  newest" or "Save mine anyway". Leaving with unsaved changes asks first.
- AC4: **Delete.** The owner can delete any of their own skills: a small confirm sheet, then the usual 8-second
  **Undo** toast; nothing is deleted until the toast ends.
- AC5: **Built-in skills** can be read but never changed or deleted, and are always used.
- AC6: **No on/off switch.** Every skill in the list is always used (BR-22). The old switch is gone.
- AC7: **Trees, branches, apples, leaves** (UX-14): the Skills branch has two apples, **Your skills** and **Add a
  skill**, each with a leaf; writing, reading and editing a skill each have their own address under the branch, with a
  breadcrumb, a big Back on phones, and deep links and reloads that work.
- AC8: A change counts from the next AI call that loads skills (for a clip job, the next job); nothing is redeployed.

- AC1: A Review screen lists every clip waiting for a decision, newest job first, with a badge count in the navigation.
- AC2: Each clip plays in place (vertical player), and shows its hook, moment type, score, source timestamp (with a
  link to that point in the source when there is one), checklist and captions.
- AC3: Captions can be edited before confirming.

### BR-08 Confirm each clip before anything is posted
"If I click confirm on each video, then you will upload each video to those social media accounts."
- AC1: Nothing is ever posted without the owner pressing **Confirm** on that clip.
- AC2: Confirm creates one post per enabled platform and queues it for publishing.
- AC3: **Decline** removes the clip and deletes its video files. It is offered with an 8-second Undo first (UX-13 AC7);
  the request is sent only when the Undo window passes.
- AC4: Confirm and Decline (once its Undo window has passed) are final for that clip and each shows clear feedback.

- AC1 (phase 1): Confirmed posts are stored with status `pending_integration` and the app says "Waiting for the account connection".
- AC1b: A waiting post goes out once its account is connected (no tap needed), and the Library gives a place that is
  set up since its own **Post now** ([CONTRACTS.md §17.6, §33.6](CONTRACTS.md#176-tokens-and-real-posting)).
- AC2 (phase 2): A queued post is uploaded through the platform's official API and gets its public URL.
- AC3: Every upload is sent from Clip Factory as a file; a retried step never posts twice; when posting fails the clip
  says why in one sentence and what to press ([CONTRACTS.md §17.6](CONTRACTS.md#176-tokens-and-real-posting)).

### BR-10 Connect social accounts (phase 2)
"This is a process to connect the social media accounts, of course. But we're gonna hold off that for now."
- AC1 (phase 1): Settings › Posting › Accounts lists YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and X as "Not connected"; the Connect
  button explains that connecting arrives in the next phase (`501 not_implemented`).
- AC2 (phase 2): Each platform connects through its official sign-in (OAuth), tokens are stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
- AC3: Settings › Posting › Set up posting replaces Accounts (the old address redirects); see BR-23.
- AC4: Connect opens the platform in the same tab and comes back with confetti and "Connected as …", or with one plain

- AC5: Disconnect shows an 8-second Undo and keeps the keys, so **Connect again** works later.

### BR-11 48-hour performance check feeding learnings
From "2 days after we've uploaded to the social media on the clips" (see interpretation I-01).
- AC1: When a clip is posted, its clip flow waits 48 hours (a durable wait that costs nothing while waiting) and then
  checks every post of that clip.
- AC2: The check stores views, likes, comments and shares on the post through the same stats refresh as BR-20, so it
  never goes over a platform's limit (phase 2 for real numbers).
- AC3: (Changed 2026-11-18, CONTRACTS.md §16.12.) Once a day Clip Factory freezes each post's day-7 views, finds the
  clips that did much better than that creator's normal on that platform and turns what they share into lessons;
  active lessons reach every job as "Prior learnings". The one-sentence 48-hour learning is retired.
- AC4: The Insights screen lists the learnings and the posts with their numbers.
- AC5: After the check the clip is remembered with its numbers in the learning memory (NFR-14), so later jobs and the
  review screens can find it.

### BR-12 Job control
- AC1: The owner can cancel a queued or running job.
- AC2: A failed or cancelled job can be retried from the beginning; an already downloaded source is reused.
- AC3: A job whose agent stops responding is picked back up on its own within about 6 minutes of its last heartbeat,
  from the moments and clips it already saved, at most twice; only then is it marked failed with "Making the clips
  stopped. Tap Try again to pick up where it left off." (job-flow callback heartbeat timeout, no scanning watchdog;
  CONTRACTS §30)

## Non-functional requirements

### NFR-01 Everything runs on AWS
- AC1: Web hosting, API, agent, storage, database, scheduling and sign-in are all AWS services in one account.
- AC2: The owner's computer is not needed for any step.

### NFR-02 Serverless architecture
- AC1: No EC2 instances, no always-on containers, no VPC, no servers to patch: CloudFront, S3 (web, media),
  S3 Vectors, Cognito, API Gateway (HTTP, WebSocket and REST APIs), Lambda (plain and durable functions), DynamoDB
  with Streams, SSM Parameter Store, one EventBridge rule (the stats tick, BR-20), AgentCore Runtime, Bedrock,
  Transcribe, CloudWatch and SNS.
- AC2: Idle cost is close to zero (pay per request and per stored byte). Services with a standing minimum charge are
  not deployed (OpenSearch Serverless, [ADR-25](DECISIONS.md#adr-25-s3-vectors-for-the-learning-memory-opensearch-not-deployed)).
- AC3: "The entire infrastructure should be serverless, meaning CloudFront, S3 buckets, DynamoDB, OpenSearch if we're
  using that, S3 vectors, API gateway, WebSockets, HTTP, REST API on those API gateways, and Lambda, and durable
  functions in Lambda." Each of these is used for a real job (OpenSearch is shown as an option, not deployed), see
  [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md#services-and-why-each-one).
- AC4: All backend code is Python and all infrastructure is Terraform ([ADR-26](DECISIONS.md#adr-26-python-for-every-backend-terraform-for-every-resource-serverless-only)).

### NFR-03 Model: Claude Fable 5.1
- AC1: The agent and every Claude call use Claude Fable 5.1 through the global cross-region inference profile
  `global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1`.
- AC2: The model id lives only in `config/models.json`.

### NFR-04 Infrastructure as code, set up completely
- AC1: Every AWS resource is defined in Terraform under `infra/`; nothing is created by hand except the OIDC deploy role.
- AC2: A first deploy into an empty account creates the whole system, including the owner's user.

### NFR-05 CI/CD
- AC1: Every push and pull request runs lint, type checks, tests and a Terraform validation (`ci.yml`).
- AC2: Every push to `main` deploys production (`deploy.yml`) through a GitHub OIDC role; no long-lived AWS keys.
- AC3: The owner supplies only `CF_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` (variable) and `CF_OWNER_EMAIL` (secret).

### NFR-06 Sign-in with Cognito, about once a month
"Make sure that the access token is refreshed every 15 minutes, but the refresh token should be refreshed every month."
- AC1: Access and ID tokens last 15 minutes and refresh silently.

### NFR-13 Live updates
"API gateway, WebSockets."
- AC1: While the app is open and connected, a change to a job, clip, post, learning or week's picks appears on screen within about
  2 seconds of being written, without a refresh.
- AC2: Only the signed-in owner's own changes are sent, in the same shape as the HTTP API; internal fields never reach
  the browser.
- AC3: The connection is opened with the owner's access token, which is never written to any log.
- AC4: A dropped connection is invisible to the owner: the app reconnects by itself (1 s up to 30 s apart), refetches
  what is on screen, and polls while disconnected. No error message is shown for it.
- AC5: Without a live connection (mock mode, old config) the app works exactly as before with polling.

### NFR-14 Learning memory
"S3 vectors."
- AC1: Every clip the agent makes is stored as a vector of its text (moment type, hook, title, summary) with the
  owner's id, status, platforms and score band.
- AC2: Before choosing moments, the agent receives up to 8 of the owner's posted and measured clips most like the new
  source ("What worked before"), as advice, never as a rule.
- AC3: 48 hours after posting, the clip's memory is updated with its numbers.
- AC4: If the memory cannot be read or written, jobs and screens carry on without it.
- AC5: The memory has no standing cost (pay per request and per stored vector).
- AC6: Clips the owner starred as best of the week are marked `best` in the memory and are offered to the agent
  first (BR-21).

### NFR-15 Durable workflows
"Lambda, and durable functions in Lambda."
- AC1: The job workflow (start agent, wait, finish or fail) and the clip workflow (posts, publish, wait 48 hours,
  metrics, learning, memory) each run as one Lambda durable function, written in Python.
- AC2: Starting a workflow twice for the same job run or clip run never runs it twice.
- AC3: Waiting (for the agent, for 48 hours) uses no compute; no queue, schedule or scanning job is needed.
- AC4: A deploy never changes a workflow already in flight.

### NFR-16 Public webhook endpoint
- AC1: Platforms reach `{hooks_url}/hooks/{platform}` and `{hooks_url}/oauth/{platform}/callback` on a separate REST
  API, so the app's own API accepts only the owner's token.
- AC2: The endpoint is throttled (10 requests a second, burst 20), stores events for 14 days, and never logs query
  strings (OAuth codes).
- AC3: Meta and YouTube verification challenges are answered today; TikTok and X answer "not implemented" until phase 2.

### NFR-17 Stay inside every platform's limits and costs
"Whatever the lowest limit is for each API."
([CONTRACTS.md §16.4](CONTRACTS.md#164-configplatformsjson-read-by-terraform-and-by-the-code-copied-into-the-zip))
- AC1: The automatic refresh and the Refresh button share one budget per platform, kept in DynamoDB and reserved with
  one conditional write before every request, so two refreshes at once can never go over a limit together.
- AC2: YouTube: at most 7,000 of the 10,000 daily quota units are used for numbers (3,000 stay for uploads); a quota
  error pauses YouTube until the quota resets (08:00 UTC).
- AC3: TikTok: at most 300 requests a minute (the limit is 600); a "rate limit exceeded" answer pauses it for a minute.
- AC4: Instagram and Facebook: the `X-Business-Use-Case-Usage` header is read after every call; at 75 % of any
  counter, or on a throttle error (80002, 80001), the platform pauses for at least the time Meta gives, and a throttled
  call is never retried (retrying makes Meta's block longer).
- AC5: X: at most 1,000 requests per 15 minutes (the limit is 3,500), and an estimated spend cap of **$10 a month**;
  re-reading the same post on the same UTC day counts as free. At the cap, X pauses until the next month, and Settings ›
  Posting › Set up posting says so in one line.
- AC6: Batches use each platform's largest request size (YouTube 50 ids, TikTok 20, Instagram and Facebook 50, X 100).
- AC7: Only metrics the platforms still support are read: never Meta `impressions`, `plays`, `post_impressions_unique`
  or `total_video_impressions*`; X video views come from the video's own `view_count`, never from impressions.
- AC8: Platform tokens never reach DynamoDB, logs or responses; no request is made for a platform without a connected
  account (phase 1: no request at all).
- AC9: An expected failure (limits, a deleted post, an expired token) never stops the poller and never repeats in a
  tight loop: the post waits its normal interval and shows the reason in plain words.

### NFR-18 The help assistant is private, capped and easy to turn off
([CONTRACTS.md §19.6](CONTRACTS.md#196-api-in-cf-prod-api-file-apisrcclipfactory_apirouteshelppy-package-apisrcclipfactory_apihelp),
[ADR-38](DECISIONS.md#adr-38-bm25-over-vectors-for-help-and-the-model-is-optional),
[ADR-39](DECISIONS.md#adr-39-help-runs-in-cf-prod-api-with-claude-haiku-55-through-the-eu-profile))
- AC1: Questions and answers are never stored and never logged; each request logs one line with its request id and
  outcome only.
- AC2: The model is Claude Haiku 5.5 through the EU inference profile, so help questions are processed in EU Regions
  only. Its id lives only in `config/models.json`.
- AC3: At most 6 questions a minute and 60 an hour; at most 2,000 model answers per 30 days, after which answers come
  from search only. A rate-limited question is never retried automatically.
- AC4: A deploy flag (on in prod) and a kill switch that needs no deploy. When the switch is off, the launcher
  disappears and the app stops answering from its own copy too.
- AC5: Help runs inside `cf-prod-api` (two routes, same JWT); the HTTP API keeps its single proxy route; the only new
  permission is `bedrock:InvokeModel` on the EU profile and its six EU models.
- AC6: The model call has timeouts (3 s connect, 10 s read, no retry) and a deadline, so a slow model falls back to
  the plain answer instead of hanging; the browser gives up after 27 s and answers locally.
- AC7: The server reads the knowledge only from the app's own address (the meta tag in `index.html`, an `/assets/`
  path on the same origin), caches it 10 minutes and falls back to the copy bundled in the Lambda.
- AC8: The knowledge never contains keys, ids, emails or infrastructure words; a test fails if it does.
- AC9: A failing model raises an alarm (10 failures in an hour) to `cf-prod-alarms`.

- AC2: Clicking a disabled control, an error toast, or a failed action plays the owner's **error sound** (default

- AC5: Changing the pick in Settings changes the sound everywhere in the app at once, with no reload.

### UX-10 Phone, browser and desktop install
- AC1: The app works in any modern browser on phone and computer.
- AC2: It installs as a PWA on the phone home screen and on the desktop (Chrome, Edge, Safari).
- AC3: On Mac and Windows it can also be downloaded as a desktop app (BR-15, NFR-11).

### UX-11 Plain English
- AC1: Every label, message and error is a plain sentence a non-technical owner understands.

"Once you click reload, there should be a nice UI to where it goes fast to 80% or to 70%, and then it's almost like
it's slow in and slow out, but in the middle, it's really quick ... so that the user's dopamine is still being hit."
- AC1: Pressing Reload turns the bar into a progress bar that runs from 0 to 75 % in about 0.8 s on an ease-in-out

- AC2: While the new version installs (service worker update, fresh files), the bar keeps creeping forward slowly; it

- AC3: When the new version is ready, it eases to 100 %, a small sparkle plays, and the page reloads by itself.

- AC5: With reduce motion on, the bar simply fills, with no sparkle.

## Out of scope for this phase

- Posting automatically the clips that were kept before a platform was connected (they stay "Waiting for connection";
  [roadmap](ROADMAP.md#phase-2-social-integrations)).
- Webhook signature checks and acting on webhook events.
- OpenSearch Serverless (an option, not deployed).
- Browsing, joining or applying to Content Rewards campaigns inside Clip Factory (that stays on Content Rewards; its
  tools offer no way to do it). Reading and following joined campaigns is in scope (BR-25).
- Content Rewards campaigns that want drafts first or the brand's own sound, and sending proof of views for the owner
  (Clip Factory reminds him and says how).
- Money from TikTok, Instagram and X (their tools tell apps nothing about it), and what left Content Rewards for Whop
  and the bank (its tools list no withdrawals); they say "not available" with where to look (BR-27).
- Turning a normal clip into a campaign clip in place (a copy is made instead, BR-28 AC5), and campaigns that want
  their own picture on top of the video (a hard stop "Pick another campaign").
- More than one user.
- A custom domain.
- Signed and notarized desktop builds, and a store listing for phones (NFR-11 AC5, [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md#later)).

## Platforms

- youtube: label YouTube; numbers: Updates daily; numbers refresh at most every 15 min; manual refresh every 5 min; Connect asks for: youtube.readonly, yt-analytics.readonly, youtube.upload
- tiktok: label TikTok; numbers refresh at most every 15 min; manual refresh every 5 min; Connect asks for: user.info.basic, video.publish, video.list
- instagram: label Instagram; numbers: Can take 2 days; numbers refresh at most every 30 min; manual refresh every 30 min; Connect asks for: instagram_basic, instagram_manage_insights, instagram_content_publish, pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement
- facebook: label Facebook; numbers: Can take 2 days; numbers refresh at most every 30 min; manual refresh every 30 min; Connect asks for: pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement, pages_manage_posts, pages_manage_engagement, read_insights, business_management
- x: label X; numbers refresh at most every 15 min; manual refresh every 5 min; Connect asks for: tweet.read, users.read, tweet.write, media.write, offline.access

## AI models for clip jobs (Settings › Clip making › Clips › AI model)

- Claude Fable 5.2: Smartest. Best at finding moments.
- Claude Fable 5.1: Very smart. The usual one. (the default)
- Claude Opus 5.5: Smart and quicker.
- Claude Sonnet 5.5: Good and fast. Costs less.
- Claude Haiku 5.5: Cheapest, fastest. Simpler picks.

## Kid-proof words

### 12.4 Kid-proof UX (a 6–8-year-old must manage it)
* One obvious next step per screen (one vermilion CTA), big targets (≥ 48 px on phones), icon + word on buttons
  (except the phone tab bar), short plain words (no jargon: "Make clips", "Upload", "Throw away"), friendly empty states
  that say exactly what to tap, no dead ends, every error says what to do next, destructive actions undoable for 8 s
  (toast with Undo) instead of scary dialogs, forms that can't be submitted wrong (paste button, auto-detect link,
  inline hints), progress always visible, celebrations on success.

parts.title: Every place in Settings
parts.text:
Settings › Clip making › Clips (/settings/clip-making/clips): How many clips, how long a video can be, and which AI makes them.
  - How many clips (#clip-count): Clip Factory makes between your fewest and most clips each time.
  - Longest video (#longest-video): For a longer video, only the first part is used.
  - AI model (#ai-model): The AI that finds your moments and writes your captions. Your pick is used for your next clips.
Settings › Clip making › Skills (/settings/clip-making/skills): Teach Clip Factory how you like your clips.
  - Your skills (#your-skills): Clip Factory uses every skill here, every time it makes or checks anything.
  - Add a skill (#add-skill): Write one by answering three easy questions, or upload a skill file from your computer.
Settings › Clip making › What it learned (/settings/clip-making/learned): Lessons from your clips that did best.
  - What it learned (#what-it-learned): Lessons from clips that did much better than normal. Turn one off or delete it.
Settings › Clip making › Streamers I follow (/settings/clip-making/streamers): Follow YouTube, Twitch and Kick streamers and see who is live.
  - Follow a streamer (#follow-streamer): Paste their link or type their name. Only follow streamers who said you can make clips.
  - Who you follow (#streamers-followed): Who is live right now, and when a stream ended or a new video came out.
  - Clips by itself (#clips-by-itself): Each video it makes costs the same as one you paste. Coming in the next update.
  - Twitch and Kick keys (#streamer-keys): A grown-up does this once. YouTube works without it.
Settings › Clip making › YouTube help (/settings/clip-making/youtube): For when YouTube blocks a video.
  - YouTube cookies (#youtube-cookies): You can skip this. Add them only if YouTube blocks a video. Export them from a private window, then close it.
Settings › Posting › Set up posting (/settings/posting/setup): Connect YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and X.
  - Set up posting (#setup-posting): Do each one once. After that Clip Factory posts by itself.
  - The setup list on your screen (#setup-todo): It stays at the top right until each place is set up or skipped. Skipped ones wait here.
  - Who can see your YouTube clips (#youtube-privacy): Everyone, only people with the link, or only you.
  - What X costs (#x-cost): About 1.5 cents a post. It stops at $10 a month.
  - Content Rewards (#contentrewards): Get paid by brands for your clips. Set it up once.
  - Your campaigns (#campaigns): The Content Rewards campaigns you added, and what to do next.
Settings › Posting › Where clips go (/settings/posting/where): Pick the places your clips go.
  - Upload clips to (#post-to): Pick at least one place.
Settings › Posting › My settings (/settings/posting/my-settings): How each clip goes up: public, open for comments, never made for kids.
  - YouTube (#my-settings-youtube): Everyone can see it, Gaming, tells your subscribers. Never made for kids.
  - TikTok (#my-settings-tiktok): Everyone can see it; comments, Duet and Stitch on. You still tap Use my settings on each clip.
  - Instagram (#my-settings-instagram): Reels also show in your feed.
  - Facebook (#my-settings-facebook): Reels on your Page are public. Nothing to pick.
  - X (#my-settings-x): Everyone can reply. Used once X is set up.
Settings › Posting › Money (/settings/posting/money): How close you are to getting paid, and real money each app reports.
  - Money dashboard (#money-dashboard): The money each app reported, and what each clip earned.
  - Your country (#money-country): Some apps have different goals in each country. Pick yours once.
  - YouTube (#money-youtube): How close you are to the Partner Program, and what YouTube says you earned.
  - TikTok (#money-tiktok): How close you are to Creator Rewards.
  - Instagram (#money-instagram): Followers against the goal for Gifts.
  - Facebook (#money-facebook): Followers, minutes watched and Meta's estimate once it is checked.
  - X (#money-x): Premium and verified followers against the goal.
  - Content Rewards money (#money-contentrewards): Money from brand campaigns, in their own numbers, and how to move it to your bank.
  - Getting your money out (#money-payouts): Each app pays you itself. Add your bank or PayPal inside each app.
Settings › Look & feel › Sounds (/settings/look-and-feel/sounds): Turn sounds on or off, and pick your two sounds.
  - Sounds (#sounds-on): Sounds only play when you tap, never when you scroll.
  - Click sound (#click-sound): Plays when you tap something that works.
  - Error sound (#error-sound): Plays when something can't be done.
  - Try it (#try-sounds): Hear your two sounds on a pretend Sign in button.
Settings › Look & feel › Motion (/settings/look-and-feel/motion): Less moving around on the screen.
  - Reduce motion (#reduce-motion): Turns off confetti, page moves and the moving background.
Settings › Look & feel › Background (/settings/look-and-feel/background): See-through glass, your picture or your colours.
  - What's behind the glass (#background-kind): Pick See-through, Picture or Colours.
  - Glass strength (#glass-strength): Clear shows more of what's behind. Frosted shows less.
  - Background picture (#background-picture): Use your own picture behind the glass. It stays on this device.
  - Background colours (#background-colours): Mix up to 3 colours behind the glass.
Settings › App & account › Get the app (/settings/app/get-the-app): Open Clip Factory like any other app.
  - Get the app (#get-app): Put Clip Factory on this device, next to your other apps.
Settings › App & account › Notifications (/settings/app/notifications): Get told when your clips are ready, even with the app closed.
  - This device (#notify-device): Turn notifications on here. On iPhone, open Clip Factory from your Home Screen first.
  - Clips ready (#notify-ready): When your clips are done.
  - It stopped (#notify-stopped): When a video stops and needs Try again.
  - Picked up again (#notify-resumed): When a video that stopped starts again by itself.
  - Every step (#notify-steps): One card per video that changes as it works: the step and the clip. It can buzz often.
  - Content Rewards news (#notify-contentrewards): You're in, send-now reminders, approvals, proof and money.
  - Number on the app icon (#notify-badge): Shows how many videos are working right now.
  - Lock Screen widget (#notify-lock-screen): Lock Screen widgets only come with App Store apps. Your notifications show there instead.
  - Send a test (#notify-test): Sends one to this device so you can see it work.
Settings › App & account › Updates (/settings/app/updates): Your version, and checking for a new one.
  - This version (#this-version): New versions arrive by themselves.
  - Check for updates (#check-updates): Looks for a new version right now.
Settings › App & account › Ask (/settings/app/ask): Web search, and what Ask can do for you.
  - Web search (#ask-web-setup): Lets Ask read today's web pages, for steps that change.
  - What Ask can do (#ask-status): Ask answers any question, knows your app and reads your files.
Settings › App & account › Account (/settings/app/account): Who is signed in, and signing out.
  - Signed in as (#signed-in): The email you use to sign in.
  - Sign out (#sign-out): Signs you out of Clip Factory here.
